claim: The rewritten acceptance criterion ends 'Neither closed profile schema has a field for those six', but the same sentence locates four of the six on provider_instance_profile, which is itself a closed profile schema. Read as written the criterion contradicts itself; the claim is only true if 'closed profile schema' silently means the matrix and adapter profiles alone, which the criterion never says.
evidence: FGI-015 criterion: 'the issuer by Plans/GitHub_API_Auth_and_Flows.md and oauth_registration_ref, the allowed host by normalized_host and api_base_path, the non-secret token owner by the three credential_ref and credential_key_ref fields ... and the Git-versus-API roles by git_transport_state, api_state, transport_api_independent and credential_access. Neither closed profile schema has a field for those six'. In Plans/forge_integration_contracts.schema.json, $defs/provider_instance_profile has additionalProperties false with 30 properties, all 30 required, and carries oauth_registration_ref, normalized_host, api_base_path, credential_ref, git_transport_state, api_state, transport_api_independent and credential_access - i.e. the named carriers for issuer, allowed host, token owner and Git-versus-API roles. The two definitions the claim must mean are $defs/provider_matrix_profile (14 properties, all required, additionalProperties false) and $defs/provider_adapter_profile (23 properties, additionalProperties false); the ledger's findings shard record 26 names exactly those two ('the matrix profile has fourteen properties' and 'the adapter profile's auth methods is a flat enum array'), but the criterion does not.
suggested_repair: Replace 'Neither closed profile schema' with 'Neither the provider matrix profile nor the provider adapter profile', which is what record 26 means and what makes the sentence true.

claim: The issuer fact is mapped to Plans/GitHub_API_Auth_and_Flows.md, a GitHub-owner document that records no issuer for any of the other twelve provider profiles FGI-015 governs. The surface named cannot carry the fact for most of the matrix, so the criterion is still unverifiable for those providers - the defect R-07 was raised about, moved from a coined surface to a real but wrong one.
evidence: FGI-015 canonical_text: 'the issuer by Plans/GitHub_API_Auth_and_Flows.md and by provider_instance_profile.oauth_registration_ref for a registered instance flow'. Case-insensitive counts over Plans/GitHub_API_Auth_and_Flows.md at 211442d028: 'issuer' 0, 'Entra' 0, 'Azure' 0, 'Microsoft' 0, 'GitLab' 0, 'Bitbucket' 0 (only Forgejo 7 and Gitea 7 occur). The second carrier, $defs/provider_instance_profile/properties/oauth_registration_ref, is {oneOf:[{type:null},{$ref:non_secret_ref}]} - a nullable reference, and the text itself limits it to 'a registered instance flow', which excludes GitHub direct OAuth, Azure Services Entra and the guided scoped PAT paths the same unit enumerates. FGI-015's own provider list does state the issuer facts, verbatim 'Microsoft Entra is the Azure Services issuer rather than a new legacy Azure DevOps OAuth registration'.
suggested_repair: Map the issuer to FGI-015's own provider list, which already states it per provider, and keep Plans/GitHub_API_Auth_and_Flows.md and oauth_registration_ref as the GitHub-specific and registered-flow carriers they are.

It defers to the Azure fixture work ADO-003 names, but that question's recorded scope does not include a container or repository-kind fixture, so the branch's own rule that an obligation with no validator surface is recorded as a question is not met for this one.
evidence: ADO-001 validation_surfaces: 'Recognising a TFVC container from the provider's own repository-kind data has no fixture ... that criterion is stated and not yet falsifiable, and writing the fixture waits on the same Azure fixture work ADO-003 names.' Section 3 repeats it. q-019 summary is 'Which Azure review, policy and check fixtures get written, and when?' and its detail scopes the work to 'the Azure review revision, thread, vote, policy-evaluation and check fixtures'; q-020 covers only SCS-023, F3-561, FGI-018, FGI-019 and FGI-020; q-017 and q-018 are the second research pass and the status-to-policy join key. The operating capsule's new negative constraint, added by the same commit, reads 'say that there is no validator surface and record the question instead'.
suggested_repair: Widen q-019's summary and detail to include the TFVC container-recognition fixture, or raise q-021 for it, and point ADO-001 at the question by id as the five planning units point at q-020.

claim: The design atom's exact_tokens were rewritten from the token the fix commit dropped to two tokens the new prose happens to contain. That is what keeps compile witness 2 green, so for this atom the witness no longer tests the compile against an independent record, and the audit trail no longer shows that a token once recorded as exact was abandoned.
evidence: records/design_atoms.jsonl atom-azure-az-26 goes from "exact_tokens": ["point-of-consent"] at 7380013f04 to ["auth_methods", "credential_access"] at 211442d028; FGI-015's preserved_exact_tokens makes the same substitution. python3 scripts/pm-ledger-compile-witness.py ... --base 4f5eda0d18 reports 'witness 2 exact tokens: 53 item tokens; missing from every owner unit's prose 0'; point-of-consent occurs in no Plans file at the tip except the findings shard, so the witness would have counted it missing had the atom kept it. Mitigating: point-of-consent was this branch's own coinage - it occurs nowhere under Plans/ at base 4f5eda0d18 - and cycle 1 asked for its removal, so the substitution is defensible on the merits.
suggested_repair: Keep the new tokens but record the drop, for example a correction or a line in record 26 saying point-of-consent was withdrawn by review rather than silently replaced.
